context.description: Ikara-Flinders Ranges National Park covers about 95,000 hectares of folded ranges in South Australia's semi-arid north, roughly 450 km from Adelaide. Its centrepiece is Wilpena Pound, the amphitheatre of mountains the Adnyamathanha call Ikara, meaning meeting place. The Brachina and Bunyeroo gorges cut through the Heysen Range, and ancient rock paintings and engravings survive at Arkaroo Rock and Sacred Canyon. The park is co-managed by the Adnyamathanha and the state, and the resort at Wilpena is the only accommodation inside it.

context.description: Quorn is a railway town at the southern end of the Flinders Ranges. The Pichi Richi Railway has run heritage steam and diesel trains from its station to Port Augusta since 1973, on the original Ghan route that reached Quorn in 1879. Walking tracks, including the Heysen Trail, climb the ranges around the town, and the stone ruins of Kanyaka Station lie about 33 km north.

context.description: Port Augusta sits at the head of Spencer Gulf, where the roads to the Flinders Ranges and the outback meet. The Wadlata Outback Centre covers the Aboriginal and European history of the outback, and the Australian Arid Lands Botanic Garden shows desert plants across red sands on the city's edge. A restored 1882 water tower gives views over the town, the gulf and the ranges.

context.description: Port Pirie is a port city on Spencer Gulf, home to the Nyrstar smelter, whose chimney is visible from miles around. A self-guided heritage trail links more than 30 sites, and a mural trail and the National Trust museum add more of the city's story. The long wooden Port Germein Jetty, Telowie Gorge and Beetaloo Reservoir all lie within a short drive.
